page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v7 is an AMD EPYC 9V45-powered general-purpose virtual machine offering 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores with 2 threads per core) operating up to 4.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The system provides 384.0 GB of memory maintaining a 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU) and includes 5,669 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without dedicated GPUs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16.

Benchmark measurements place the instance consistently in the top tier across raw processing, memory throughput, and I/O-intensive workloads. In stress-ng, it achieved scores of 3,792.98 (single-core) and 176,145.96 (multi-core), alongside a PassMark CPU score of 117,050.24. Memory operations yielded 311.62 GB/sec read and 174.65 GB/sec write on uncached 256MB blocks, paired with a cached small-block bandwidth of 9,486.57 GB/sec. Data processing capability is highlighted by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 610.83 GB/sec and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 41.25 GB/sec.

For practical application tiers, the instance delivers high transaction processing and throughput, evidenced by 140.26 million Redis SET operations per second and 91.12 GB/sec static web serving throughput. CPU-based inference workloads achieve 5,540.41 tokens/sec prompt processing on small models (135M) and maintain 57.76 tokens/sec text generation on medium models (7B), though prompt processing drops to an average 25.81 tokens/sec on large 70B models due to the absence of hardware accelerators.

Given its combination of 96 compute threads, massive local NVMe scratch storage, and balanced memory allocation, the D96ads_v7 provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale enterprise workloads. It is well-fitted for relational databases, extensive in-memory caching layers, high-volume web serving, large-scale data compression and decompression pipelines, and CPU-driven batch processing.
